reader.requirement: At --std 85, the RELATIVE KEY data item named in the ACCESS MODE clause must carry the relative record number both ways: the program's value selects the record for random READ, WRITE, REWRITE, DELETE and START, and the system stores the number into it on a sequential WRITE and on a format 1 READ, for every unsigned-integer description the format allows (any usage, any size, qualified).

edition-consulted.switches: below 2002 the RELATIVE KEY must be a phrase of the ACCESS MODE clause (refuses a standalone clause, COBOL0900)
out-of-range key on a random WRITE: '24' below 2014, '34' from 2014 (DialectBehavior.RelativeWriteKeyOutOfRangeIsPermanentError)

reader.edition-search: grep Edition|DialectLevel|DialectBehavior over FileControlBinder*.cs, KeyedIoEmitter.cs, RelativeConnector.cs, PlaceTable.cs; the key's staging (FileSetRelativeKey) and store-back are edition-free.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: at 85 the RELATIVE KEY is a phrase of ACCESS MODE only (2002+ allows a standalone clause); a random WRITE with key 0 gives 24 at 85 and 34 at 2023 (no INVALID KEY at 2023); the transfer of the number is the same code
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witness uses DISPLAY keys with dynamic and random access; it does not exercise sequential access with a key (WRITE/READ storing the number), a binary or qualified key, the digit-capacity statuses 14/24, zero or largest key values, or the SR2/SR3 refusals

probes.printed: WS1 00 0001 / WS2 00 0002 / WS3 00 0003 / RS1 00 0001 AAAA / RS3 00 0003 CCCC / RD2 00 00BBBB / ND3 00 0003 00CCCC / RD0 IK 23 / RDMAX IK 23 / R3 00 00BBBB / R3B IK 23 / W4 IK 24 10 / W4 LAST 24 9 / W5 00 / R4 END 14 9
probes.expected: sequential WRITE stores 1,2,3 (§1985:VIII.4.9.4 GR11a), READ stores the number (§1985:VIII.4.5.4 GR14), START by K1 OF KG, binary 9(4) COMP key, key 0 and 999999999 are 23, the 10th sequential write with a 1-digit key is 24 and the READ of record 10 is 14 (§1985:VIII.1.3.4): matches

probes.printed: COBOL0863 for each: 'shall be an unsigned integer without the symbol P' (signed, PP, X(3), 9(3)V9); 'shall not be defined within a record description of file' (own record)
COBOL0863 ACCESS RANDOM with no RELATIVE KEY; COBOL0900 a RELATIVE KEY clause that is not a phrase of the ACCESS MODE clause requires COBOL-2002
probes.expected: refused: the 1985 format prints RELATIVE KEY as a required phrase of RANDOM/DYNAMIC

probes.printed: 85: W IK 24 / R IK 23; 2023: no W IK line, R IK 23
probes.expected: 85: invalid key 24 for a write outside the file's boundaries (§1985:VIII.4.9.4 GR15)

reader.notes: The key's place (PlaceTable.RelativeKeyOf) is staged into the connector before each keyed verb and stored back after sequential WRITE and format 1 READ; both directions, the digit-capacity statuses and the description refusals hold at 85. Refusal diagnostics cite the 2023 clause numbers.

refuter.evidence: ext_seq2.cob: relative SEQUENTIAL file with RELATIVE KEY opened EXTEND after records 4 and 7 exist: WRITE stores 8 then 9 into the key (E1 00 008, E2 00 009; §1985:VIII.4.9.4 GR12, the level-2 extend arm the reader did not exercise), sequential READs store 4, 7, 8, 9. keyalias.cob: key qualified KA OF GA inside a group set by a group MOVE "<003>" reads record 3, READ NEXT stores 7 seen through the group (<007>) while the same-named KA OF GX stays 000; PACKED-DECIMAL key inside a REDEFINES of PIC X reads record 7; BINARY 9(4) key on sequential READ stores 3 then 7. keylink.cob: key in the LINKAGE SECTION of a called program receives 2 after two sequential WRITEs, seen by the caller (M 002). keyocc.cob: key subject to OCCURS refused COBOL0863. ext_seq.cob: WRITE without INVALID KEY and no USE refused COBOL6826, correct by §1985:VIII.4.9.3 SR3. cite.py: OK §1985:VIII.4.9.4 GR12; OK §1985:VIII.2.4.4 GR6 (reader's).
